interaction.prompt: You have a tight gap and inside position on the carrier near the dot. Tap the lane you should steer them into, away from the middle.

mc.stem: You are the defenseman with a tight gap and inside body position on the puck carrier near the faceoff dot. What is the correct read?
opts: Keep your stick on the ice and steer the puck carrier down the boards
Back into the slot and give the puck carrier the middle of the ice
Dive at the puck and hope the carrier cannot step around you
Stop your feet and wait for the puck carrier to choose first

feedback.right: Yes. A tight gap at the dot is a chance to finish the angle. Keep skating, protect the middle, and steer them to the low-danger boards.
feedback.wrong: Backing off or diving gives up the middle, the most dangerous ice. Keep your feet, protect the middle, and steer them down the boards.

tip: With a tight gap and inside position, keep your feet and steer the carrier to the boards, away from the middle.
why: A tight gap at the dot is a chance to finish the angle. Keeping the feet moving and protecting the middle steers the carrier to lower-danger ice.
